author: nonretail_writer
central_thesis: Going into the pending January CPI print, the relief rally (S&P 500 +1.45% to 4,587.18, VIX 19.96) sits on top of a rate-driven regime in which the 2-year has risen 46 bps over 20 observations in a bear flattening, so the book should favour pricing-power cash generators (energy, banks, materials, offshore China internet, Australian banks, Polish banks only with a hedge) over long-duration growth and bond proxies, treating Russia-Belarus escalation and an Iran deal as the two opposite energy tails.
sources_policy: Every fact comes from a 2022-02-10 frozen-feed headline (read via tools/digest.py for 2022-02-10, topic and grep modes) cited in the same part, or from the 2022-02-10 market card (tools/showcard.py); card values are quoted as shown with the tags (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-09), (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-09) and (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-09) for crypto. Each citation was checked against its headline wording, category window and timestamp (all strictly before 2022-02-10T00:00Z); previews are used only as previews; no estimates, flows, positions or episode details were invented. Each ID is used at most twice (275 distinct IDs). Process disclosure: during the initial survey a shared scratchpad digest file was overwritten mid-read by another date's digest; everything read from that file was discarded, the own-date digests and card were regenerated into a date-named private directory, the card was confirmed byte-identical to the own-date card, and every citation was re-derived and checked directly against the 2022-02-10 feed. No other date's feed, card, spec, draft or note was used. Verifier: python3 tools/verify.py --nonretail 2022-02-10 passes with 0 fails and 0 warnings at 8,967 body words.
known_ambiguities_omitted: n0796 (CNBC, 'Dow slides 500 points as yields spike following red-hot inflation report'), stamped 2022-02-09 08:00, describes the post-CPI session after the cutoff: misdated/after-cutoff, not cited.
US January CPI outcome, consensus and market reaction: pending at the cutoff; only the 'inflation data in focus' preview (n1343) is used, no release date or estimate is asserted.
BoJ fixed-rate purchase operation (about 04:00 UTC on 10 February): pending and without an own-date preview headline, so not mentioned.

Twitter, Coca-Cola, PepsiCo, AstraZeneca, Unilever, Zillow, Affirm and Cloudflare results: pending; only preview or positioning headlines are cited (n0543, n0775, n0869, n0618) and no outcomes or dates are stated; Affirm and PepsiCo appear only through card prices; AstraZeneca and Zillow are not mentioned.
Kellogg (n0819, 'labor strike to eat into margins'): reads as a results preview and the results may fall on the report date, so it is used strictly as a preview with no outcome claimed.

Siemens-Koerber logistics sale (n0855, 'agrees ... 1.15 bln euro deal'): announcement time relative to the cutoff cannot be confirmed from the day-granular stamp, so the 'imminent -sources' headline (n0856) is used instead and no deal value is quoted.

Numeric spot-FX in Polish and FX headlines (n1759 EUR/PLN level, n1591, n1590, n1644 Czech koruna comparison, n1222 EUR/USD) not quoted; n1759 is used only for the direction of the zloty after Glapinski's conference; yen discussed only as a rate-differential mechanism, with no level or move claimed.

Promotional or low-quality items avoided: n0376 (Motley Fool 216%-257% hypergrowth list), n0690 (metaverse stocks to buy), n0517 (Moomoo 'gain 50%'), n0899 (Fundstrat bitcoin $200k forecast), CoinMarketCap/CoinGecko price pages, n0881 (TradingView EPS page), n0078 (ig.com most traded), n1173 (Bored Panda on Chipotle tips).
n1162 (Yahoo Finance, Apple to enable crypto payments with Tap to Pay): speculative relative to Apple's own announcement (n1121), not used.
Super Bowl LVI crypto and NFT advertising (FTX bitcoin giveaway n0920/n0938, Bud Light NFT imagery n0915): pre-game promotion only; the game and ad airing are after the cutoff, not used.
n0805 (FOREX.com, Alibaba rallies on SoftBank announcement) sits awkwardly with n0611 (SoftBank looking to sell Alibaba shares); used only as stated, without characterising the announcement.
SoftBank's own quarterly results: only the Bloomberg preview (n0717) is in the feed, so results are not described.

Polish MPC February hike size and new reference rate: no own-date headline states them; only 'highest in nearly 9 years' (n1723) and Pekao's 50 bp forecast (n1625) are used; anti-inflation shield details beyond n1552 not stated.

Russia-Ukraine: Belarus drills (n1439), the UK foreign secretary's Moscow trip (n1442) and the EU letter (n1441) are treated as pending; no invasion or later sanctions are asserted. n1792 (Truth Social launch expected by end of March) not used.

Conflicting figures kept with their own sources: Barron's $3.6 billion bitcoin seizure (n0682) quoted, BBC's '$4bn' (n0956) used only for 'record-high'; Arm deal value $40bn (Guardian n0698) and $66 billion (CNBC n0719) each quoted only with its own outlet.
Reviewer flag: tirzepatide is attributed to Eli Lilly in XLV; the cited headline (n1907) names the drug, not the company.
No verifier WARNs remain; no repeated sentences, calendar-wording or long-paragraph flags.
